head: bf5a7907157be6c1e30801e485faa0d9fbdfd290
method: grep-driven scan over backend/app, frontend/src, backend/tests, frontend tests, backend/scripts, frontend/scripts (evidence harness), backend/app/ai/skills (prompts) and the living docs (AGENTS, README, RULES, ARCHITECTURE_MAP, AI_CONTEXT_BUNDLE, ROADMAP, OPEN_ISSUES, THESIS_ARCHITECTURE, THESIS_READINESS, CORRECTNESS, TEST_TIERS, DEMO_RUNBOOK, RUN_NAMING, docs/architecture, the first 130 lines of CURRENT_STATE), one target item at a time, then reading each hit in context. Historical artifacts under docs/evaluation are G by definition and are cited only as examples.

classes.A_SAFETY_INVARIANT: safety rule that must hold everywhere
classes.D_CONFIGURABLE_DEFAULT: default that may change without changing the contract
classes.F_BASELINE_TEST_ENVIRONMENT: the machine/browser a measurement ran on
classes.G_HISTORICAL_MEASUREMENT: a value observed in one run
classes.I_TEMPORARY_IMPLEMENTATION_LIMIT: declared limit of the current implementation

required_examples.GPU Tesla T4: NA-01 — no GPU model is recorded in the repository; a GPU is F (baseline), never a contract.
required_examples.Chrome 154: NA-02 — recorded environment of the W12 run (G); other browsers are NOT_MEASURED.
required_examples.3·3·5·5·5·10: NA-13 — historical measurement (G); acceptance = semantic coverage + observable delta, no fake steps.
required_examples.cache/candidate: NA-22…NA-25 — read from the repository (app.main, EVALUATION_CANDIDATE.json); task-prompt values are claims.
required_examples.colour: NA-30/NA-31 — the semantic role is the contract; hex values come from tokens.

items.statement: No GPU model string (e.g. 'Tesla T4') is recorded anywhere in the repository. Browser gates run headless Chrome with software WebGL (ANGLE/SwiftShader) or --disable-gpu; real-GPU frame times exist without a model name, and phone GPUs were never measured.
items.rationale: A GPU is the machine a measurement ran on. It can be recorded as the baseline of a performance number; it is never a product contract. No performance claim may name a GPU it was not measured on.

items.statement: W12 records 'system Chrome 154.0.8037.59, --headless=new, ANGLE SwiftShader'.
items.rationale: This is the recorded environment of one run. It does not mean other browsers or versions are unsupported, and it does not mean they are supported: they are NOT_MEASURED.

items.statement: Browser scripts locate Chrome at 'C:/Program Files/Google/Chrome/Application/chrome.exe' (BrowserSession also tries /usr/bin/google-chrome); there is no environment override.
items.rationale: The install path of the baseline machine. It is an environment fact, not a contract.
items.repair: Add one override (CHROME_PATH) to BrowserSession and record the resolved executable and version in every run manifest; legacy one-shot scripts need no change.

items.statement: Tooling assumes Windows: venv interpreter at .venv/Scripts/python.exe, Git Bash/PowerShell commands, no make. lock_cache_identity.py branches on sys.platform explicitly.
items.rationale: Baseline development environment. Product code has no OS branch.

items.statement: test_raw_response_identity_reproduced asserts that D:/tmp/live_retry_evidence/PRISM_SCHEMA_LIVE_P01_raw_response.json exists. The file lives outside git (verified on the baseline machine) and the test has no skip or marker, so it runs in the default pytest and in T3.
items.rationale: The default suite passes only on the machine that holds that directory; on a clean checkout T3 fails for a reason unrelated to the product. AGENTS.md §4 forbids committing raw model output, so the file cannot simply be vendored.
items.repair: Move the check behind an opt-in marker (same pattern as -m postgres) that reports NOT_PORTABLE_EXTERNAL_EVIDENCE when the file is absent, and record the hash check as a manual verification step. Never skip silently.

items.statement: One-shot measurement scripts default to personal paths (C:/Users/<user>/.gemini/..., D:/tmp/...).
items.rationale: These record where a historical run read or wrote. They are not used by the test suite.
items.repair: Parameterise only if a script is reused; record the path actually used in the run manifest.

items.statement: The six-family browser suite measures desktop 1440x900 (DPR 1) and mobile 390x844 (DPR 2).
items.rationale: Measurement viewports declared in a registry. Product code has no viewport constant (grep of backend/app and frontend/src finds none). Other sizes are NOT_MEASURED, not unsupported.

items.statement: Older certification scripts hard-code 1440x900 or 1440x1000; diagnose-responsive.mjs takes --viewports.
items.rationale: Baseline of historical certifications.
items.repair: New gates take viewports from a registry (the generic-tier-a pattern), never from a constant.

items.statement: HUONG = [8, 3, 6] is the default view direction; chonHuongNhin picks the actual direction per scene from an azimuth x elevation grid scored by projected area, depth and vertex/edge separation.
items.rationale: A presentation default with a per-scene selection on top; it never feeds geometry state.

items.statement: GOC_NHIN_THAM_CHIEU / NGUONG_GOC_NHIN (view-quality thresholds) are calibrated on one reference cuboid.
items.rationale: A threshold calibrated on a single family is a family-specific rule. Shapes that differ from a box (regular tetrahedron, cone apex, sphere) were not part of the calibration.
items.repair: Recalibrate on one case per shape class (pyramid-like, prism-like, cone-like, sphere-like) and keep the calibration set in the gate's registry.

items.statement: buildObject3D defaults cameraPosition to new THREE.Vector3(8, 3, 6), a second copy of HUONG.
items.rationale: Two copies of one presentation constant can drift apart.

items.statement: Frozen camera identity for the registered human expectations; transferred to new cameras only under DECLARED_CAMERA_CHANGE.
items.rationale: Identity of a historical measurement, kept byte-identical.

items.statement: W12 records construction steps 3·3·5·5·5·10 for triangular pyramid, triangular prism, rectangular pyramid, cuboid, cube and cross-section.
items.rationale: A count observed on one candidate. Acceptance comes from semantic coverage and an observable change per step, not from a number; adding steps to reach a number would be a fake step.

items.statement: The browser gate derives the expected step count from the trace of the same envelope (step_count_matches = observed == trace length).
items.rationale: Frame k <=> trace[k] (#31) and the geometry-timeline partition (#35): the count is derived, not pinned.

items.statement: Compiler tests pin exact step counts per family ({cuboid: 9, cube: 11, square_prism: 10}, 11 construction steps for the prism, 8 view steps).
items.rationale: Regression snapshots of hand-written per-family statement sequences. A generic formation plan will change these numbers by design.
items.repair: Replace with ordered semantic-coverage assertions per shape class plus a derived count; migrate, do not delete.

items.statement: No product branch reads a vertex label; labels appear only in docstring examples.
items.rationale: AGENTS.md §3 (no hard-coded vertex labels) holds at HEAD; grep of backend/app and frontend/src finds no branch on a literal label.

items.statement: Fixture expectations list labels (e.g. A, B, C, D, S) per scenario.
items.rationale: Expected values of a fixed fixture, not a product rule.

items.statement: The compiler supports six named families and writes one hand-made statement sequence per family (bien_dich, _bien_dich_prism, _bien_dich_rectangular_pyramid, _bien_dich_cuboid).
items.rationale: The family list is a deliberate slice of the compiler route (not the default route). The per-family sequences are the root cause of W12-H1/H2: the triangular pyramid and prism never received the height, lateral-edge and top-face steps the rectangular paths have.
items.repair: One formation plan per shape class, derived from topology roles and shared by every family (preregistered for W14).

items.statement: The analyze schema closes solid_topology to solid_kind {prism, pyramid}, base_shape {rectangle, square}, lateral_structure {right, oblique}, solid_subkind {cuboid, cube, right_square_prism}.
items.rationale: Closed family enums at the model-facing contract. There is no way to say 'regular', 'equilateral triangle', 'apex above the base centre' or a curved solid here.
items.repair: Topology roles instead of family names (base polygon kind, apex-foot relation, regularity, lateral direction); a model-facing change, so it needs its own measured wave.

items.statement: Product capability is one coarse row per kind ('polyhedron' supported covers pyramids, prisms and boxes).
items.rationale: Single authority for what the product may show as supported. Its granularity is coarser than the W13 matrix; the matrix does not override it.

items.statement: No case identifier (p1…p7, n1…n4, c7a, e4, gm_10…) appears in product code.
items.rationale: AGENTS.md §3 holds at HEAD (grep).

items.statement: The designated cache-bump test asserts CACHE_VERSION == '105'.
items.rationale: Deliberate ceremony (bump in one commit with its reason); the value is read from code at review time.

items.statement: Five further tests pin '105' and one keeps a growing allow-list ('100'…'105').
items.rationale: Undocumented copies of a live value: every bump must find them, and a missed one fails for a reason unrelated to the test's subject.
items.repair: Read app.main.CACHE_VERSION or the identity lock; keep only the ceremony test pinned.

items.statement: The browser suite pins product_commit_sha / product_tree_sha and refuses a mismatch.
items.rationale: A measurement is bound to an exact candidate on purpose. The value must come from EVALUATION_CANDIDATE.json at measurement time, never from a prompt or a document.

items.statement: Task statements carry HEAD, cache, candidate, schema and default mode.
items.rationale: Values in a task statement are claims about a moment. W13 re-read all of them from the repository (Phase 0) and they matched; the repository is the authority.

items.statement: Living state docs quote run-scoped test totals (e.g. pytest 6443 at 442584cf).
items.rationale: A test total belongs to one run and one commit and must cite it. W13 architecture documents carry no test totals.

items.statement: Hand-offs record how many commits a wave created.
items.rationale: Historical record of a wave; no rule depends on a commit count.

items.statement: W11 'refrozen once'; W12 'frozen three times'.
items.rationale: How often a wave refroze is history. The invariant is different: the candidate must match the last commit touching backend/app or frontend/src before anything is measured (freeze_evaluation_candidate.py --verify). No test or script assumes a single refreeze (grep).

items.statement: --verify compares product_commit_sha and the MEASURED_SYSTEM_PATHS tree hash.
items.rationale: Measurement identity: refreeze after every product commit, as often as needed.

items.statement: Causal role colours (target, newly built, numerical given, intermediate, context, given point) live in one role table shared by renderer and CSS, with a sync test.
items.rationale: The ROLE is the contract (blue = being looked at, dark orange = numerical given, …); the hex value is a token value that may change without changing the contract.

items.statement: The neutral type palette (derived point, line, surface, mesh, edge ink, polygon/section amber) and the lights are hex literals inside the view; the former token module scene3d-tokens.ts no longer exists.
items.rationale: A second palette outside the token authority; a gate that reads tokens cannot see it drift.
items.repair: Move the type palette into a token/role module with a sync test; keep the type roles as the contract.

items.statement: The W12 hue gate classifies pixels into orange/blue bands (s 0.45, l 0.2–0.85, hue 10–50 / 205–235).
items.rationale: A classifier threshold with a known-answer window, not a colour contract.

items.statement: Neutral views draw a section in amber.
items.rationale: Presentation default; the user marked it a design question (W12-D1), not a defect.

items.statement: Legacy sample previews and the variables view carry hex literals.
items.rationale: Presentation literals in legacy components outside the geometry renderer.

items.statement: The compiler places the right-angle vertex at the origin, legs along two axes and the apex on the normal; every length comes from the FactGraph and the coordinates are declared LAYOUT_DERIVED via model_assumption.
items.rationale: Placement is a free choice of frame (presentation); the metric comes from GIVEN facts. Policy: layout must stay scale-free or separate from the metric proof.

items.statement: The synthesis prompt tells the model to choose the frame (base in z = 0, perpendicular edge along z) and to use model_assumption only for HOW to place a named object.
items.rationale: A layout convention for the model. The channel it opens is the open assumption issue below.

items.statement: A LAYOUT_DERIVED or model_assumption coordinate can fix a dimension the problem does not state; the volume follows from it (probe: prism without 'AD = 5' served V = 30 through both channels).
items.rationale: The rule 'a layout choice is free' is applied to a choice that carries a metric the answer depends on (ISSUE-ARCH-ASSUMPTION-CHANNEL-UNSTATED-DIMENSION).
items.repair: Preregistered assumption/default policy (VISUAL_DEFAULT / MODEL_ASSUMPTION / DERIVED_VALUE / GIVEN_VALUE) with acceptance criteria; implementation is W14.

items.statement: PLANE_DISPLAY_SIZE = 6 remains the fallback size of a plane patch when no bounded points frame it.
items.rationale: Presentation fallback; the per-scene frame (khungMatPhang) is used whenever bounded points exist.

items.statement: Provider backoff, a 60 s vision timeout and short UI notice timers.
items.rationale: Operational defaults; none decides a geometric result.

items.statement: BrowserSession bounds and counts relaunches (TRAN_MO_LAI = 2) but a lost DevTools response is awaited forever.
items.rationale: An unbounded wait in a measurement tool: W12 had to kill a hung run by hand.
items.repair: Per-call timeout with a named failure (PAGE_NOT_LOADED style), counted like relaunches.

items.statement: The kernel decides every predicate exactly over Fraction (plus Radical for measures); no epsilon.
items.rationale: Exact arithmetic is the thesis claim: a tolerance would hide the class of error the system exists to refuse.

items.statement: hf(float) returns Fraction(x).limit_denominator(10**9); its docstring says floats are converted 'by their exact binary value'.
items.rationale: The docstring contradicts the code, and the code is a silent entry point for approximate decimals: a JSON float coordinate becomes an exact-looking rational. Whether any gate stops approximate coordinates for shapes whose ideal coordinates are irrational is NOT_MEASURED.
items.repair: Measure first (0-call probe: a regular tetrahedron written with decimal coordinates). Then either refuse non-source decimals in coordinates or state the 1e9 rationalisation as a contract.

items.statement: Postcondition comparison uses abs(got - expected) < 1e-9 only when one side is a float.
items.rationale: Legacy float path; exact values compare with ==.

items.statement: Renderer epsilons (1e-6…1e-12), a 10-significant-digit camera key and a 0.5 px product/oracle tolerance.
items.rationale: Presentation numerics after the exact boundary; they never feed geometry state.

items.statement: DEFAULT_MAX_STEPS = 300 bounds program execution.
items.rationale: Bounded execution is a safety invariant; the number itself is a configurable budget.

items.statement: The grammar card has a byte budget raised with a written reason each time.
items.rationale: A budget, not a semantic invariant (same status as the old max_objects = 20).

items.statement: MAX_SEMANTIC_PROGRAM_ATTEMPTS = 3 (one initial synthesis plus repairs).
items.rationale: A bound on provider spend per request is a safety rule; the value is a budget.

items.statement: Hidden-line classification considers only the faces of the edge's own solid (occluders default [o]).
items.rationale: Declared limit (ponytail note); scenes with several overlapping solids need occluders.

items.statement: RequestContract carries one solid_topology; the compiler emits one solid.
items.rationale: SINGLE_SOLID_ONLY on the contract/compiler route (v1 matrix). The LLM route may construct several solids in one program.

items.statement: canonicalEdgesOf and occludingTriangles accept only type 'solid' with faces; curved solids neither get classified edges nor occlude polyhedral edges.
items.rationale: Occlusion was built for polyhedra; curved solids draw a camera-dependent outline instead.

items.statement: FactGraph node kinds: point, segment, plane, triangle, pyramid, prism, measurement_request.
items.rationale: The compiler route is polyhedron-only; curved solids exist only on the LLM route.

items.statement: The production synthesis prompt (program_skill_for -> geometry_program_generator) still says an oblique plane through a cylinder or cone 'cannot be expressed', while the IR has intersect_plane_curved_ellipse (cylinder 2026-09-07, cone 2026-09-08).
items.rationale: A model-facing absolute contradicted by the IR and by the grammar card the same prompt is sent with. The final acceptance still served both ellipse cases, so the card wins today; the contradiction remains.
items.repair: Correct the prompt in a wave that may change the model surface (prompt hash, CACHE_VERSION decision, measurement).

items.statement: Living docs still state 8 expressions · 6 statements · 5 measures, CURVED_GEOMETRY_SUPPORT = NONE, curved and non-convex solids as deliberate gaps, 'convex polyhedra only, no curved surfaces'.
items.rationale: Contradicted by code (11 · 9 · 7 per the sync-locked identity row; curved.py; nonconvex foundation; product_capability.py).
items.repair: W13 adds a correction banner to CURRENT_STATE §3/§4 pointing at the authorities. README, THESIS_ARCHITECTURE and the v1 matrix are listed for a documentation wave (v1 is an immutable snapshot).

items.statement: Every point lives in Q^3; irrational quantities exist only as measures (Radical a·√b·π^k).
items.rationale: A deliberate exactness design whose consequence is a capability limit: a figure that has no rational placement (an equilateral triangle in z = 0 needs √3; a regular pyramid given by base and lateral edge usually needs an irrational height) cannot be built exactly.
items.repair: Preregistered: deterministic placement-feasibility check with a fail-closed code first; then evaluate similarity layouts with a Radical scale factor and Q(√d) coordinates.

items.statement: Visible/hidden spans and the product/oracle evidence cover canonical polyhedral edges; segments and sections delegate to the edge owner; circles, ellipses and curved outlines are not in the CPU classifier or the oracle evidence.
items.rationale: Correct for polyhedra; curves are NOT_MEASURED in w09–w12 evidence.

items.statement: A segment label counts only when it stands right before '=' or 'bằng' (or 'XY có độ dài v'); a number without such a label is accepted as a standalone value for any representative edge.
items.rationale: A closed grammar without fuzzy matching is the intended contract (no guessing at the gate).

items.statement: Measured: 'AB dài 5 cm' binds no segment, so a program declaring AC = 5 passes the GIVEN check (standalone_wrong_segment).
items.rationale: A labelled length the reader does not recognise falls into the standalone rule, so the value can be attached to the wrong segment without any gate noticing.
items.repair: Safe normalisation: read 'XY dài v' as a labelled length (closed phrase, no fuzzy match); preregistered for W14 with this probe as its red baseline.

items.statement: Measured: in 'AB = AC = 5' only AC is bound; declaring AB = 5 is refused with SOURCE_EVIDENCE_CONFLICT.
items.rationale: Fails closed (false refusal), so it is a coverage limit, not a soundness defect.
items.repair: Read chained equalities as one value for every segment in the chain.

items.statement: A plane equation is read only with a plane phrase within 48 characters before '='.
items.rationale: Documented window of a closed reader; unreadable equations stay unchecked (declared limit).

items.statement: The scope gate routes by word clues per obligation, with a parity test derived from the checker registry.
items.rationale: Closed table with a derived parity guard; phrasings outside it fail closed at scope (coverage limit, measured history in STATUS_LEDGER).

items.statement: Derived points are recognised by 'gọi/lấy … là' (≤ 40 chars) and 'X là trung điểm|hình chiếu|giao điểm|trọng tâm|chân đường|tâm|điểm đối xứng'.
items.rationale: Phrasing coverage limit; other lead-ins rely on the segment-division invariant.

items.statement: Coordinates: decimal comma, name after the triple, 'x_A = …', 2D and irrational coordinates are not read (declared by a green limit test).
items.rationale: Fail-open when unreadable, fail-closed when contradictory (contract); the unread forms are a coverage limit.

items.statement: Scene3D needs WebGL; without it the canvas shows a message instead of a figure.
items.rationale: A capability requirement with a defined fallback.

items.statement: Browser gates need a Chromium that speaks the DevTools protocol.
items.rationale: Capability requirement of the harness; the install location is F.

items.statement: README states Python 3.12 and Node 20+; W12 ran Python 3.12.10 and Node v24.13.0.
items.rationale: Minimum versions are requirements; the observed versions are the baseline (F).

items.statement: pytest and vitest make zero real provider calls; the guard sits at the network edge.
items.rationale: Offline-first safety invariant; never patched.

items.statement: DEFAULT_MODE stays LLM_ONLY until all 20 migration gates pass.
items.rationale: Governance safety invariant (MIGRATION_CHECKLIST).
